question: can knowing you moved separate self-caused change from the world's?
status: PARTIAL — works for rotation, not for forward motion

measured_shift_over_0.45s.note: turn_left and turn_right should be large and opposite; phase-correlation confidence during turns 0.25-0.29 vs 0.998 standing still

why: the camera spins far enough in 0.45s (~200 mouse counts) that the two views are unrelated; no shift model bridges unrelated images
calibration_behaviour: honest — it reports gain 0 (cancelling does not help) rather than pretending; the one nonzero gain (mouse+x 8.0, top of grid) made the residual worse, 0.0217 -> 0.0247
eye_defect_found: 85% of frames the eye reported FRESH were pixel-identical duplicates (21,156 of ~24,800). Desktop Duplication reports desktop change, not window change. Every frame rate quoted through that flag this session is inflated.
next: capture with total rotation per sample interval small enough to stay the same scene (order 10-20 mouse counts per 0.45s), then re-run

clear_capture.footage: clear_170306: 5,166 usable frames, 183s, 51 recorded boundaries; 32,378 frames dropped as OCCLUDED and 14,718 as duplicates — the earlier captures had no such filter
clear_capture.trackability: turn_left +0.62px, turn_right -0.71px (large and OPPOSITE), confidence 0.85; travel -0.04 at confidence 0.463 (expansion, as expected); still 0.00
clear_capture.verdict: the body input raises signal-to-chance 1.6x -> 2.2x (+38%) while suppressing recall. Real but modest, and the first time it has helped on real footage.
clear_capture.why_travel_fails: a shift model represents rotation; forward motion is radial expansion and the crude scale approximation (1 + 0.01*div*g) does not capture it — the calibrator honestly returns gain 0 rather than pretending

supersedes: the earlier UNTESTED verdict; all four prior captures were occluded and are withdrawn
